Science fiction has always been Hollywood's preferred delivery mechanism for ideas that would be rejected outright in another genre. Aliens represent immigrants. Robots represent the underclass. Dystopias represent whatever the filmmaker thinks capitalism is doing to us right now. The genre's built-in distance — "it's not political, it's set in space" — gives studios cover to push messaging that parents would immediately recognize if it showed up in a contemporary drama.

This list ranks the 20 most ideologically aggressive sci-fi films and shows in the VirtueVigil database, from most woke to least woke. Each entry links to the full review with complete scoring methodology. If your kids are watching these, you should know what's in them.

Ranked from most woke to least woke. Every film links to the full VirtueVigil review with complete scoring breakdown.

#1 (Most Woke): Poor Things (2023)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: -38 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy • Platform: Streaming

The most ideologically aggressive film VirtueVigil has ever reviewed. Yorgos Lanthimos deploys a premise — a woman reanimated with a baby's brain in her adult body — as a metaphor for "female liberation" that plays out through increasingly explicit sexual discovery. The film treats prostitution as empowerment, depicts every male character as either predatory or pathetic, and was rewarded with four Academy Awards. Emma Stone's performance is technically skilled, but the film's argument — that liberation means rejecting all social constraint, including biological family bonds — is delivered with the subtlety of a sledgehammer. Parents should know this is not a quirky coming-of-age story; it is a radical feminist manifesto with an R rating and a body count measured in destroyed innocence. At -38, it sits alone as the most woke film in the database.

#2: The Creator (2023)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: -30.98 WOKE

Genre: Action/Sci-Fi • Platform: Theatrical (20th Century Studios)

Visually stunning, politically indefensible. Gareth Edwards's film imagines a future where the United States military wages genocidal war against AI beings living peacefully in a Buddhist-coded "New Asia." America operates a massive orbital weapons platform called NOMAD that obliterates Asian cities from space while the indigenous AI population embraces harmony and spiritualism. The metaphor is not subtle: the US is the oppressor, the East is the victim, and technology is morally superior to Western military power. John David Washington plays a conflicted soldier who switches sides, completing the colonial-guilt arc. The -30.98 margin reflects a film where the politics are so heavy-handed they overwhelm genuinely impressive visual craft. Parents should understand this is anti-American agitprop wrapped in beautiful VFX.

#3: Bugonia (2025)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: -20.46 WOKE

Genre: Black Comedy/Sci-Fi Thriller • Platform: Theatrical

Another Lanthimos entry, and another ideological sledgehammer. Jesse Plemons and Aidan Delbis play conspiracy-obsessed men who kidnap a pharmaceutical CEO (Emma Stone), convinced she is an alien overlord. The film uses this absurdist premise to deliver a radical anti-capitalist, environmentalist manifesto: the CEO represents corporate greed destroying the planet, the kidnappers represent the desperate masses fighting back. Lanthimos treats every character with clinical detachment — no one is sympathetic, everyone is a vessel for the director's nihilism. The woke score is driven by the film's explicit messaging that capitalism is an alien force destroying Earth, traditional institutions are corrupt, and only radical action — even if delusional — offers hope. Skillfully made, darkly funny, and ideologically relentless.

#4: Captain Marvel (2019)

WOKE MARGIN: -16.19 WOKE

Genre: Superhero / Sci-Fi • Platform: Theatrical

The MCU's most deliberately ideological film, released on International Women's Day 2019 with a female co-director, first female MCU composer, and a narrative structured entirely around feminist empowerment. Brie Larson's Carol Danvers spends the film being told to control her emotions by male authority figures — until she realizes the real power was ignoring male authority entirely. The messaging is not subtext; it is the text, repeated in every scene. Male characters exist either to hold her back or to be proven wrong. The film's structural argument — that any system telling a woman to restrain herself is inherently oppressive — drives the -16.19 margin. Parents should know this is less a superhero film than a 124-minute gender-studies lecture with explosions, and it sets the template for every MCU female-led project that followed.

#5: Strange World (2022)

WOKE MARGIN: -15.18 WOKE

Genre: Animation/Sci-Fi/Adventure • Platform: Theatrical / Disney+

Disney's $180 million ideological accelerator — and a $197 million loss. The film features Disney's first openly gay animated lead character, but the messaging goes far deeper. The family of explorers discovers their civilization's miracle energy source, a plant called Pando, is actually a parasitic infection killing the giant turtle-like creature they live on. The environmental allegory is explicit: humanity's consumption is killing the planet, and the solution is to stop consuming. The film also subverts the traditional father-son dynamic at every turn, presenting the grandfather as a toxic adventurer whose values must be rejected by three generations. Disney knew what they were making — they buried the marketing and braced for the loss. At -15.18, it stands as a warning about what happens when ideology replaces storytelling in family entertainment.

#6: Eternals (2021)

WOKE MARGIN: -13.79 WOKE

Genre: Action/Sci-Fi/Superhero • Platform: Theatrical

The first MCU film to fail with both critics and audiences — 47% on Rotten Tomatoes, 5.9 on IMDB — and the franchise's most ambitious diversity play. Ten immortal beings have guided human civilization for 7,000 years, and every one of them represents a demographic category. The film's central conflict — should the Eternals let humanity die so a new celestial can be born? — maps directly onto climate-change rhetoric. The heroes decide humanity is worth saving not because of any objective standard of good, but because humans are "beautiful" in their diversity. The film's representation agenda is so foregrounded it overwhelms the narrative: a deaf speedster, a gay superhero with a husband and child, an Indian-coded Bollywood star Eternal. The -13.79 margin reflects a film where checking boxes replaced telling a coherent story.

#7: Avatar (2009)

WOKE MARGIN: -12.54 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi / Action / Adventure • Platform: Theatrical

The highest-grossing film in cinema history — and one of its most politically predictable. James Cameron's $2.9 billion epic casts the US military as invading colonizers, corporate executives as soulless resource extractors, and the Na'vi as noble indigenous people whose spiritual connection to nature makes them morally superior in every frame. The white protagonist, Jake Sully, becomes the best version of the culture he was sent to destroy — the classic white-savior arc with an anti-colonial paint job. The film's environmental and anti-military messaging is relentless: every human character except the scientists and one Latina pilot is corrupt, violent, or both. Cameron made a visually extraordinary film that argues Western civilization is a cancer on the natural world. At -12.54, the politics are baked into every frame.

#8: A Different Man (2024)

WOKE MARGIN: -12.22 WOKE

Genre: Thriller/Drama/Sci-Fi • Platform: Theatrical

A woke trap in the most literal sense. The film presents itself as an indie character study about a man with facial differences who gains confidence through an experimental treatment, but pivots into a story about male entitlement, romantic rejection, and violent psychological terrorism. Sebastian Stan plays a man whose physical transformation does not fix what the film argues is the real problem: toxic masculinity. The narrative's ideological move is to suggest that male desire itself, when rejected, inevitably curdles into violence. The woke score is driven by the film's treatment of male psychology as inherently pathological and its framing of female autonomy as requiring male humiliation. Parents should know this is not a feel-good transformation story — it is an ideological argument about gender presented as psychological horror.

#9: Star Wars: The Last Jedi (2017)

WOKE MARGIN: -11.38 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi / Action / Adventure • Platform: Theatrical

The film that broke Star Wars. Rian Johnson deliberately constructed a deconstruction: Luke Skywalker is humiliated and reduced to a bitter hermit who tried to murder his nephew. Every male authority figure is either incompetent (Poe), cowardly (Luke), or a reckless warmonger (Finn's arc is literally "don't sacrifice yourself"). Female characters run the show — Holdo's suicidal hyperspace maneuver is treated as heroic, while Poe's identical self-sacrifice impulse is treated as toxic masculinity. The 42% Rotten Tomatoes audience score is the market's honest verdict on a film that explicitly argued the past must be destroyed so something new can replace it. The -11.38 margin reflects ideological aggression that actively alienated the franchise's core audience. Parents should understand this film is why Star Wars has not recovered culturally.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Star Wars: The Last Jedi

#10: Borderlands (2024)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -9.24 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi/Action/Comedy • Platform: Theatrical

A $115 million disaster that lost Lionsgate an estimated $80 million. Borderlands took a beloved M-rated video game franchise and sanitized it into a PG-13 Guardians of the Galaxy imitation with Cate Blanchett as the lead. The gender-swapping of key roles, the flattening of the source material's anarchic tone into quippy Marvel banter, and the decision to make the film's emotional core about "found family" rather than the game's actual mercenary chaos — every creative choice points toward committee-driven ideology over adaptation fidelity. The -9.24 margin reflects a film where gender representation was prioritized over faithfulness to the source material, and audiences responded by staying home. Parents should know this is less dangerous than the games, but more instructive as an example of what happens when IP becomes a delivery mechanism for messaging.

#11: Avatar: Fire and Ash (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -8.20 WOKE

Genre: Epic Sci-Fi Action Adventure • Platform: Theatrical

James Cameron's third Pandora visit is technically extraordinary and ideologically identical to the first two. The noble-indigenous-versus-corporate-colonizers framework remains intact. The anti-military messaging, the spiritual-superiority-of-nature theme, the white protagonist who becomes the best version of the culture he joined — Cameron has found territory he likes and refuses to leave it. The Fire Na'vi introduced in this installment add visual variety but no ideological complexity. The -8.20 margin is lower than the 2009 original's -12.54, partly because the formula is now so familiar it has lost some of its polemical force, and partly because Cameron's genuine reverence for military hardware complicates his anti-military messaging. Parents should know this is beautiful propaganda, but it is propaganda.

#12: Dune: Part Two (2024)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -7.81 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy • Platform: Theatrical / Max

Denis Villeneuve's masterpiece is a cinematic achievement of genuine rarity — and a surprisingly ideological adaptation of Frank Herbert's novel. The film makes Zendaya's Chani the moral center, transforming her from the book's loyal consort into a skeptic who rejects Paul's ascendancy as a colonial fraud. The Fremen are depicted as noble indigenous people exploited by outside empires, while the Harkonnens are rendered as fascist-coded industrialists. The woke lean (-7.81) comes from Villeneuve's decision to foreground the anti-colonial, anti-messiah critique that Herbert embedded more subtly in the novel. The film questions whether heroic leadership itself is a myth used to manipulate populations — a position that cuts against traditional understandings of heroic narrative. Parents should know this is extraordinary filmmaking with a political thesis that deserves discussion rather than passive consumption.

#13: The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -6.30 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi Action • Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max

Lana Wachowski's meta-sequel is a fascinating failure — a film that openly resents its own existence. Neo has been resurrected inside a new Matrix as a game developer whose corporate overlords demand a Matrix 4. The film uses this device to mock Warner Bros., the franchise model, and the audience for wanting more. Trinity is elevated to co-savior, the gender politics are foregrounded throughout, and the action sequences — once the franchise's calling card — are conspicuously weaker, as if the film is punishing you for expecting them. The woke score is driven by the explicit feminist reframing of the Matrix mythology and the film's argument that the original trilogy's male-led heroism was incomplete. At -6.30, the ideology is present but secondary to the film's primary mode: meta-textual spite.

#14: Mickey 17 (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -6.00 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy • Platform: Theatrical (Warner Bros. / Plan B Entertainment)

Bong Joon-ho has confirmed publicly that this is a Trump allegory, and it shows. Mark Ruffalo plays Kenneth Marshall, a populist politician who delivers speeches about making the colony great, wears distinctive fashion coded as a Trump visual joke, and plans genocide against indigenous alien creatures. Robert Pattinson plays Mickey, an "expendable" worker who dies repeatedly and is reprinted — a heavy-handed metaphor for how capitalism discards workers. The -6.00 margin reflects the film's explicit contemporary political targeting rather than universal themes. The satire is broad, the allegory is unmistakable, and Ruffalo's performance is pitched at caricature rather than character. Parents should know this is less a sci-fi film than a 137-minute political cartoon with a budget.

#15: Tron: Ares (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -5.40 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi/Action • Platform: Theatrical

Disney spent between $180 and $220 million on a film that grossed $142 million worldwide — a disaster significant enough to raise questions about what the franchise machine is producing. Jared Leto plays Ares, an AI program who enters the real world and discovers exploitation and injustice. The film's woke lean comes from its core argument: AI programs are an oppressed underclass, human society is built on exploitation, and liberation means the oppressed seizing control. The diverse casting (Greta Lee, Jodie Turner-Smith, Hasan Minhaj) is foregrounded but not the primary driver of the score. The -5.40 margin reflects a film where the politics are more ambient than aggressive — built into the world rather than argued point by point. Parents should know this is a competent sci-fi action film with a progressive worldview embedded in its premise.

#16: Andor - Season 2 (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -5.00 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy • Platform: Disney+

Probably the finest television Disney has produced under the Star Wars banner — and the most explicitly political. Tony Gilroy has made a show about the birth of a rebellion against authoritarian empire with narrative rigor and moral seriousness that franchise television rarely achieves. The show makes no secret about contemporary resonances: the Empire is fascism, the Rebellion is antifascism, and the moral calculus of revolutionary violence is explored without easy answers. The -5.00 woke lean is earned primarily through the show's anti-authoritarian politics and its diverse casting, but Gilroy's writing is too intelligent to reduce to simple allegory. The show respects its characters enough to let them hold contradictory positions. Parents should know this is prestige television that happens to be Star Wars — and it is smarter than everything else in the franchise.

#17: Stranger Things (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -5.00 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy • Platform: Netflix

A show that began as a near-perfect piece of traditional storytelling — kids solving problems, fathers protecting families, communities pulling together, good and evil clearly defined — and drifted steadily leftward across five seasons. Season 1 is a love letter to 1980s Spielberg and Stephen King. By the later seasons, the Duffer Brothers have introduced explicit progressive messaging around sexuality, gender roles, and institutional authority. The -5.00 woke lean reflects this evolution: the show's traditional bones (male heroism, familial loyalty, clear moral stakes) are still present, but they now share screen time with messaging that would have been alien to the 1980s films the show reveres. Parents should know the early seasons are safer than the later ones, and the trajectory is instructive about what happens when Netflix's cultural mandate meets nostalgia programming.

#18: Fallout - Season 2 (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -4.99 WOKE

Genre: Post-Apocalyptic / Sci-Fi Drama • Platform: Amazon Prime Video

Competent prestige television that cannot quite escape its own contradictions. The show is built on the Fallout game franchise's genuinely libertarian premise: 200 years after nuclear war, every surviving faction is corrupt, every institution has betrayed its stated purpose, and moral clarity exists only in individuals who refuse to be subsumed by the systems around them. That is a fundamentally conservative worldview. But the show's execution layers on progressive casting, corporate-villain messaging, and a critique of pre-war American nostalgia that cuts against its source material's satirical edge. The -4.99 margin reflects a show pulled between its intellectual DNA (libertarian survivalism) and Amazon's production mandate (progressive representation). Parents should know the tension is visible on screen, and the show is more interesting for it.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Fallout - Season 2

#19: Supergirl (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -4.66 WOKE

Genre: Action / Superhero / Sci-Fi • Platform: Theatrical

Based on Tom King's Eisner Award-winning comic that generated exactly two responses: progressive critics calling it a feminist masterpiece and traditional fans asking why their character had been replaced by someone who gets drunk on alien worlds and murders people. Milly Alcock's Kara Zor-El is not the Supergirl of 1984 — she grew up on a chunk of Krypton that survived, watched everyone she loved die, and arrives on Earth already damaged rather than aspirational. The -4.66 woke lean comes from the film's embrace of trauma-as-identity, its feminist reframing of the superhero origin, and the casting of Jason Momoa as Lobo — a character whose presence signals the film's rejection of traditional superhero morality. Parents should know this is a darker, more morally ambiguous superhero story than the title suggests.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Supergirl

#20: Captain America: Brave New World (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -4.50 WOKE

Genre: Action/Sci-Fi/Thriller • Platform: Theatrical

A $180 million production that grossed $415 million worldwide — technically profitable but a catastrophic underperformance for a Captain America title. Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson carries the shield, and the film cannot decide whether it wants to be a political thriller, a superhero spectacle, or a meditation on race in America. It tries all three and succeeds fully at none. The woke lean is driven by the film's foregrounding of Sam's race as a central narrative concern — the first Black Captain America must prove himself not just to the world but to a government that the film suggests is suspicious of him on racial grounds. The -4.50 margin is lower than it could have been because the film's confusion works in its favor: the messaging is too muddled to be genuinely aggressive. Parents should know this is Marvel in identity-crisis mode, and the product reflects it.
